summary: This article explains how animals such as monkeys, elephants, bees, ants, and Arabian wolves use sounds, movements, and smells to send each other messages.
introduce: Show the title “How Animals Talk” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: to share ideas, feelings, or information with others
an animal that hunts and eats other animals
a sound or sign that warns of danger

challengeTerms.def: to figure out what something means
a sound made with the voice

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that animals can share messages almost as well as people can? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Compare two ways animals communicate from the article, such as sounds and smells. How are they alike, and how are they different?
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review communicate, predator, and alarm, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses distinct, interpret, and vocalization to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
